# src/navigation/ — the navigation stack: the navigation mesh and its tiles, path queries, the
# funnel, the region hierarchy, flow fields, off-mesh links, local avoidance and crowds. M8.b
# section 6, tasks 6.1 and 6.2.
#
# ================================================================================================
# WHAT IS ENGINE-OWNED AND WHAT IS RECAST'S
# ================================================================================================
#
# `navigation` requires meshes "generated by voxelising source geometry and extracting walkable
# surfaces", and `ai-system` names that step as one where a proven algorithm MAY be integrated
# because it is "not differentiating". Recast is that algorithm and it is declared in
# deps/manifest.toml, gated by CY_NAVIGATION_RECAST.
#
# EVERYTHING ABOVE VOXELISATION IS THIS ENGINE'S, and the boundary is one function —
# `cy::navigation::build_tile()` in build.h. Detour, Recast's own runtime half, is deliberately NOT
# integrated: `navigation` requires navigation tiling independent of world cells, async queries
# completing on a deterministic tick, and flow fields and hierarchical refinement Detour does not
# have. See include/cy/navigation/navmesh.h for the full argument.
#
# The module therefore BUILDS AND TESTS WITHOUT RECAST. `build_tile()` has an engine-owned
# heightfield path that runs when CY_NAVIGATION_RECAST is off, and the suite exercises the same
# contract in both configurations — a boundary only one configuration compiles is a boundary that
# has never been checked.
#
# LAYER. `scene` (4), the rung src/world/, src/gameplay/ and src/graph/ each chose for the same
# reason: there is no `navigation` rung in `engine-architecture`'s table and inventing one is not
# this milestone's change to make. The dependency list is what makes the choice honest — cy::ecs for
# the components `navigation`'s "Navigation components" requirement names, and nothing above it.
# Nothing here reaches a renderer, a device or a server: a navigation mesh is cooked data and a path
# query is arithmetic over it.
# Sources are listed explicitly and never globbed: a file this list does not name is compiled by
# nothing, which reads in a review exactly like a file that passes.
set(cy_navigation_sources
    src/build.cpp
    src/components.cpp
    src/crowd.cpp
    src/flow_field.cpp
    src/hierarchy.cpp
    src/navmesh.cpp
    src/query.cpp)

# THE ONE TRANSLATION UNIT THAT NAMES AN `rc` SYMBOL, and it is compiled only when the option is on.
# `build_tile()` reaches it through `cy::navigation::detail::build_tile_recast`, declared
# unconditionally in src/recast_bridge.h and called only behind `recast_available()`, so a build
# without the option links without the definition — and without a stub that would be a second place
# the option is read.
if(CY_NAVIGATION)
    list(APPEND cy_navigation_sources src/build_recast.cpp)
endif()

cy_add_module(
    NAME cy_navigation
    LAYER scene
    ALIAS cy::navigation
    TYPE STATIC
    SOURCES ${cy_navigation_sources}
    PUBLIC_INCLUDE_DIRS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include"
    PRIVATE_INCLUDE_DIRS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src"
    PUBLIC_DEPENDENCIES cy::core-base cy::core-math cy::core-memory cy::core-values cy::ecs)

# PRIVATE, and that is the point — the same line src/backends/physics-jolt/ draws around Jolt. No
# consumer inherits Recast's include directories, so `#include <Recast.h>` does not resolve outside
# this target and an `rc` type cannot reach a header. `CY_NAVIGATION` is compiled in for the same
# target so `recast_available()` and `build_tile()`'s dispatch read one fact.
if(CY_NAVIGATION)
    target_link_libraries(cy_navigation PRIVATE cy::dep::recast)
    target_compile_definitions(cy_navigation PRIVATE CY_NAVIGATION)
endif()

if(CY_BUILD_TESTS AND EXISTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/CMakeLists.txt")
    add_subdirectory(tests)
endif()
